clue.text: Settlement has hospital in remote area

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word for a remote area

blocks.note: the tip of a landmass is its furthest, most remote point
to have something is to own it
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A frontier village boasts a hospital despite lying somewhere far from anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' reads as the main verb of the sentence, but it is a piece of wordplay sitting beside the hospital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A township is a small town or community, a place people have settled to live.

clue.text: Tank overturned near bombed restaurant

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so in a down clue it is read from bottom to top
something bombed is blown apart, so its letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tank flips over close to a dining place hit by an air raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek eating house serving simple food and wine.

clue.text: Blown coils let out liquid

blocks.note: to wind is to coil, so coils is winds
weeping lets out tears

explanation.surface: A coiled pipe sprang a leak and spilled fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Windswept describes something exposed to strong gusts, battered or tousled by the weather.

clue.text: Quiet guy fed by a witch doctor

indicators.note: something fed by another takes it in, so the following letter goes inside

blocks.note: sh is the call for silence
a guy is a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A silent fellow is given food by a tribal healer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal healer and spiritual intermediary, the role popularly called a medicine man.

clue.text: Where cop can be seen acting as guardian

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: the three letters c-o-p sit visibly across the second and third words of the phrase
second meaning: Latin for in the place of a parent

explanation.surface: A police officer appears when someone takes on the care of a child.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful pointer: the word cop is literally visible inside loCO Parentis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase describes someone who takes on a parent's responsibilities, such as a teacher or carer.

clue.text: Make mummy and me lamb stew?

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients together, so the preceding words are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A child asks their mother to cook a lamb casserole together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make mummy' reads as a child's request to cook with mother; it actually means preserve a corpse as the Egyptians did.
explanation.definitionFit: Embalming preserves a dead body with spices and resins, which is how the Egyptians produced their preserved corpses.

clue.text: Counters count without calculator?

blocks.note: the pieces in board games like draughts are men
to tally is to count up

explanation.surface: People who add up do their sums in their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counters' looks like people who count; it means game pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing arithmetic mentally means working it out in your head, with no machine to help.

clue.text: A Transcaucasian stargazer invites hugs

indicators.note: the words hug, or hold within them, the letters needed

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An astronomer from the Caucasus welcomes people with embraces.
explanation.definitionFit: An Azeri is a native of Azerbaijan, a country lying south of the Caucasus mountains.

clue.text: Madonna with Child in stonework

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the Madonna is the Virgin Mary
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A carved Madonna and Child appears in church sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: Madonna with Child is the familiar title of countless religious artworks, which makes the surface look like a straight description of a statue.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is the craft or product of building with cut stone, i.e. a mason's work.

clue.text: Row of vehicles, factories etc

blocks.note: surface reading: a line of cars and industrial buildings
setter's reading: row rhymes with cow, a din, the racket made by traffic and industry

explanation.surface: A list describing a line of cars and factories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' pretends to be a line of things; it means a loud racket.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names unwanted environmental sound from sources such as traffic and industry.

clue.text: Against getting a new vehicle

blocks.note: V, short for versus, means against
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone objects to the purchase of a fresh car.
explanation.definitionFit: A van is a covered motor vehicle used for carrying goods, so it is one kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Talented people, completely game

blocks.note: all means wholly, completely
rounders is a British bat-and-ball game, a forerunner of baseball

explanation.surface: Gifted folk are totally up for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like the adjective meaning willing; here it is the noun, a schoolyard sport.
explanation.definitionFit: All-rounders are versatile people who are good at many different things, notably cricketers who both bat and bowl.

clue.text: Troll is lonely one that carries one’s rocks

definitions.note: a definition by example: the whole phrase says Troll is an isolated instance of the answer

indicators.note: to rock something is to shake it violently, so the preceding words are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A solitary mountain troll lugs around its own pile of stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Troll is the name of Norway's research base in Antarctica, about as remote as anywhere. 'Rocks' looks like the troll's luggage but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Troll is an actual Norwegian scientific base in remote Antarctica, so it is one example of such a facility.

clue.text: Top copy with illiterate’s signature

blocks.note: to ape someone is to copy or imitate them
someone who cannot write signs with a cross

explanation.surface: A first-rate duplicate of a document is marked by someone who cannot read.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or summit of something, its very peak.

clue.text: Pay to pen column describing nipples?

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as animals in a pen, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a pillar is a column

explanation.surface: A newspaper pays to have a column written about breasts.
explanation.walkthrough: PILLAR goes inside PAY: PA(PILLAR)Y. The question mark signals that nipples stands for papillae, small nipple-like bumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Papillary means relating to papillae, the small nipple-shaped projections found on skin, tongue and other tissue.

clue.text: I’m on about creating division in moderate hate

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and rearranged
dividing something splits it apart, so the jumbled letters go into its middle

blocks.note: to abate is to lessen or moderate
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone banging on about divisive issues stirs up hatred in a moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or detest intensely, a strong synonym for hating.

clue.text: Becoming awfully crude, so hiding nothing

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the preceding letters are messed up
to hide something is to keep it inside, out of sight

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone turning terribly vulgar, concealing nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' looks like a verb, but here it is the adjective meaning fitting or seemly.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorous means in keeping with good taste and propriety, which is what becoming means as an adjective.

clue.text: See building—around the back, stuff

indicators.note: back means reading the word for stuff from its end

blocks.note: ca, for circa, means around in dates
taken as written
to lard is to stuff meat with fat

explanation.surface: Directions to a building: go round the back and you'll find some things.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is the area a bishop governs; 'See' looks like the verb for looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, the building housing the bishop's throne in that see.

clue.text: Tea cake politician put in sauce bottle?

indicators.note: put in means one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: a cruet is a small table container for oil, vinegar or sauce
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician gets doused in condiment at a tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: A crumpet is a soft griddle cake eaten toasted with butter at teatime in Britain; a cruet is the little stand of condiment bottles on a dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumpet is a spongy griddle bread toasted and buttered, a traditional British teatime treat.

clue.text: Positions offered by big name at Apple

blocks.note: first meaning: posts of employment that are available
second meaning: Steve, co-founder of the computer company

explanation.surface: Vacancies advertised by a famous technology company.
explanation.definitionFit: Jobs are paid positions of employment, and Steve Jobs co-founded and led Apple Computer.

clue.text: One’s job is to make do

definitions.text: One’s job is to make do

blocks.clueFragment: One’s job is to make do
blocks.note: surface reading: someone whose role is to get by with what is available
setter's reading: a do is a hairdo, so this person's work is creating hairstyles

explanation.surface: A worker whose role is to manage with little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make do' reads as the idiom for coping; split it and do is a hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser who cuts and styles hair produces a hairdo for each client.

clue.text: An unpleasant job not quite enough for newsreader

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a chore is a tedious task

explanation.surface: A disagreeable task falls just short of being sufficient for the person reading the news.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is the main presenter of a television news programme, the person reading out the stories.

clue.text: One unpredictable character following VW

blocks.note: first meaning: a person whose behaviour cannot be foreseen
second meaning: the letter after V and W is X, the algebraic symbol for an unknown

explanation.surface: An erratic driver tails a Volkswagen.
explanation.walkthrough: VW looks like the car maker but is just two letters of the alphabet; the next letter is X, the unknown in algebra.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a person or thing whose nature or behaviour is not yet known, and also x in an equation.

clue.text: 1000 Rand and single European currency

blocks.note: K stands for a thousand, as in kilo
R is the symbol for the South African rand
single means one

explanation.surface: A thousand South African rand and a single unit of the euro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single European currency' suggests the euro, but the definition is just the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The krone is the monetary unit of Denmark and Norway, both European countries outside the eurozone.

clue.text: This still gets used by race officials

definitions.text: This still gets used by race officials

blocks.clueFragment: This still gets used by race officials
blocks.note: surface reading: something stewards keep on using even now
setter's reading: a still is a single photograph, which judges consult when runners cross the line together

explanation.surface: Stewards at a racecourse continue to rely on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as the adverb meaning even now; it is the noun for a single photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: When a race is too close to call, officials check a camera image taken at the line to decide the winner.

clue.text: One needs one tropical bird

blocks.note: an, the indefinite article, means one
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A person requires a single exotic bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs' simply puts the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The ani is a black tropical American cuckoo, a bird found in warm climates.

clue.text: Faith is embraced by enemy of US

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside the arms of another, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: us and them are the classic opposing sides
taken as written

explanation.surface: A religion is adopted by a foe of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: US looks like the United States; it is the pronoun us, whose opposite camp is them.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in a god or gods, a religious conviction rather than atheism.

clue.text: Fear fencing that is on river most cross

indicators.note: fencing encloses a space, so the word for fear surrounds what follows
in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so that is is sent second, behind river

blocks.note: angst is anxiety or dread
R is the abbreviation for river
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Dread surrounding something by the water makes people furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fear fencing' paints a picture of a scary fence; fencing is just the instruction to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: Angriest is the superlative of angry; cross is an informal word for annoyed or irritated.
